install_tell: sudo apt install ros-jazzy-desktop && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && ros2 run demo_nodes_cpp talker  (default: Fast DDS, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0, UDP multicast on 239.255.0.1:7400, NO SROS2, plaintext on the wire)
misconfig_patterns: Default: no authentication, no encryption — any participant on the same domain on the same subnet (or reachable via Discovery Server) gets full read+write to every topic and every service
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 left at default — collides with every other ROS 2 user on the same LAN
ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY unset — multicast goes to the primary interface, often a routable subnet
UDP 7400-range port-forwarded to the public internet through misconfigured cloud security groups
Discovery Server (TCP 11811) exposed on a public cloud IP without SROS2 — direct read-write gateway to the entire fleet graph
DDS Router (TCP 11600-range) used to bridge robot fleet across regions, public-internet exposed
rosbridge_suite (WebSocket 9090) running with default auth_disabled config — full DDS bridge over plaintext WS
Foxglove Bridge (WebSocket 8765) exposed without auth — full topic publish/subscribe over WS
micro-ROS Agent (UDP 8888) exposed without auth — direct bridge into PX4 flight stack on UAV companion computer
Docker network_mode: host plus ros: image tag — DDS multicast escapes container isolation by design
SROS2 enabled but Permissions CA / Domain CA leaked in a public Git repo (search GitHub for *.permissions.xml + private key)

FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE points at an XML that disables transport encryption while DDS-Security is enabled — known XML-profile UAF / parse class vulnerabilities (CVE-2023-50725, CVE-2024-30253-30255, CVE-2024-41642)
RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_dynamic_cpp — dynamic type negotiation exposes TypeObject parsing surface (CVE-2024-41642)
ParticipantSecurityInfo builtin attributes broadcast in plaintext discovery even when crypto is on — reveals which deployments use SROS2 (a posture-classification fingerprint, not a vulnerability)

active_probe.false_positive_check: RTPS magic bytes (0x52 0x54 0x50 0x53 followed by 0x02 0x0n version) on UDP 7400-range with a valid CDR-encoded ParticipantBuiltinTopicData reply is the high-confidence identity. The string 'RTPS' alone is heavily FP'd (RTSP misindex, Yamaha RTP, log strings). Adjacent web-bridge fingerprints (rosbridge port 9090 with 'op'+'topic' JSON message shape on WebSocket, Foxglove port 8765 with /ros JSON Schema) are HTTP-discoverable confirmations. Reject if vendor_id is not in the OMG-assigned range or if the ParticipantBuiltinTopicData fails CDR deserialization.

shodan_dorks.notes: 2026-06-09 Stage -1 brief: Shodan UDP coverage is shallow — UDP 7400-range PARTICIPANT_ANNOUNCE banners do NOT appear in Shodan because Shodan does not send DDS discovery probes. FOFA is the recommended PRIMARY engine for this category: 'protocol="rtps"' and 'body="fast-dds"' yield CN robotics fleets that Shodan deprioritizes. Censys ZGrab2 has no native RTPS module as of 2026-06-09. The HTTP/WebSocket adjacent surface (Foxglove :8765, rosbridge :9090, Discovery Server TCP :11811) is the Shodan-visible front door of a Shodan-dark backend. Insight #93 honored: bare-no-port variant included. Honest population estimate: 100-800 direct DDS exposures + 1500-4000 adjacent web-bridge exposures globally.

do_not_call: Publishing to any /cmd_vel or robot velocity command topic — MOVES THE ROBOT, physical safety risk
Publishing to any *Twist, *JointTrajectory, *Pose, *JointState command-side topic — actuator control
Publishing to /initialpose or /goal_pose (Nav2) — re-localizes or re-plans navigation
Invoking any Action Server goal (*Action/_goal_request) — starts navigation, manipulation, takeoff, drop sequence
Calling set_parameters service — re-configures any node
Calling lifecycle_node transition service — turns nodes off, deactivates managed lifecycle
rosbag2 record on camera/audio/PII topics — full data exfil, not enumeration
Saturating MultiThreadedExecutor with high-rate requests — DoS the node
PX4 + micro-ROS: publishing to /fmu/in/vehicle_command, /fmu/in/offboard_control_mode, /fmu/in/setpoint_*, /fmu/in/actuator_motors, /fmu/in/actuator_servos — TAKES OFF, LANDS, ARMS the airframe
Foxglove Bridge WS: {op:'advertise'} or {op:'publish'} — same state-change risk over the WS bridge
rosbridge WS: {op:'advertise'} or {op:'publish'} or {op:'call_service'} on state-change services
DDS Router: pushing routes into a new domain — bridges adversary into operator fleet
Universal Robots URCap: dashboard service calls (power on, brake release, play) — moves the arm
data_class: robotics middleware metadata + sensor feeds + actuator command surface. Direct PII risk: low (camera/microphone topics can leak human imagery/audio, but only when subscribed — restraint = never subscribe to *Image, *PointCloud2, *Audio topics on operator hosts). Safety risk: HIGH — state-changing operations move physical robots. The schema/graph metadata (participant names, topic names, IDL type_names, node hostnames) is the -allowed finding payload; the data is not exfiltrated.
restraint_notes: Identity probe = passive RTPS multicast listen OR send a single SPDP PARTICIPANT_ANNOUNCE and receive DCPSParticipant replies. No active publish on user topics.
Graph enumeration = subscribe ONLY to the four DCPS builtin topics (DCPSParticipant, DCPSPublication, DCPSSubscription, DCPSTopic). No subscription to any user-defined topic.
For adjacent web bridges: GET / on Foxglove :8765 and rosbridge :9090 for identity. Foxglove getDataTypes is read-only and allowed; never call advertise or publish.
Compute / actuator endpoints are PHYSICAL-SAFETY primitives — NEVER call. The open-state is the finding; calling is the harm.
For drones (PX4 + micro-ROS): the /fmu/in/* command topic family is OFF LIMITS regardless of authorization. Inadvertent publish can crash the airframe.
Alias Robotics' aztarna (open-source ROS recon tool) implements the read-only PARTICIPANT_ANNOUNCE primitive correctly — reuse rather than re-implement.
ROS 1 (TCPROS / XML-RPC master on TCP 11311) is EOL since Noetic May 2025 but still in the wild; ros1 hosts are out-of-scope-for-AI-LLM but in-scope-for-substrate findings.

Insight #40 (auth-on-default shifts rightward) is UNMET here — ROS 2 has shipped open-by-default since 2017. The right-shift is happening at the deployment layer (VPN overlays, Discovery Server behind firewall, Wireguard meshes), not at the DDS layer. SROS2 adoption rate is low.
Insight #12 (shadow sweep) — when an HTTP front (Foxglove on :443) is reachable, sweep :8765 + :9090 + :11811 + UDP 7400 on the same IP.
Substrate-vs-AI/LLM categorization: Jetson Docker registry on :5000, default nvidia SSH, exposed gstreamer ports = SUBSTRATE findings, not ROS 2 findings. Categorize separately.

version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 1 (2007 - May 2025 EOL): TCPROS over central roscore master, NO auth ever
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Ardent (2017-12): DDS chosen as middleware abstraction; first ROS 2 distro
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Bouncy (2018-07): SROS2 introduced as experimental DDS-Security wrapper, opt-in
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Dashing (2019-05): SROS2 graduated; ros2 security CLI matured
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Foxy (2020-06 LTS): Fast DDS (renamed from Fast-RTPS) becomes default RMW; SROS2 stable but off by default
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Galactic (2021-05): Cyclone DDS becomes default RMW; Discovery Server unicast pattern introduced
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Humble (2022-05 LTS): Fast DDS returns as default; Discovery Server matures; SROS2 still opt-in
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Iron (2023-05): zero-copy via Loaned Messages; ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE env var introduced
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS 2 Jazzy Jalisco (2024-05 LTS): current LTS; no change to security defaults — still ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 + no SROS2 by default
